title: Egalitarian interruptible batcher with memory-aware KV throttling
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement: Continuous batching currently favors high-throughput long-lived requests (e.g., long conversations or heavy embedding streams) which can monopolize GPU memory and KV cache shards. This causes out-of-memory (OOM) events for co-located smaller short-lived requests and violates per-customer latency SLOs. Goal: design and implement an interruptible (preemptible) batcher that enforces short-term egalitarian resource allocation across customer streams while being KV-cache and GPU-memory aware. The feature should maintain or improve p50/p95 latency for latency-sensitive classes while preserving overall throughput and minimizing KV cache churn.

Scope: design runtime-level scheduling policy and KV-aware throttling heuristics, implement scheduler and runtime hooks, add telemetry/dashboards and safety controls (canary rollout, config flags). This ticket covers design, simulation, prototype on staging, and rollout tasks. Implementation will integrate with the continuous batching loop, KV cache LRU/TTL signals, and the GPU memory allocator to make preemption decisions that avoid expensive KV cache evictions and excessive kernel context switches.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler can preempt batches mid-flight at token granularity without corrupting KV cache state
Latency-sensitive class (defined by label) p95 improves or remains within 10% of baseline under mixed workload in staging
KV cache churn (evictions/sec) does not increase more than 25% under representative mixed traffic compared to baseline
No increase in OOM incidents on staging for 48-hour soak test
Feature deployable behind runtime feature-flag and per-customer policy toggles
tasks: Design doc: scheduling algorithm, KV-aware cost model, and GPU memory signals (owner: Avery)
Simulator: extend batcher sim to model token-level preemption and KV locality (owner: Mateo)
Runtime: implement preemption hooks and safe checkpoint/resume for KV cache/kv-slab pointers (owner: Mateo)
Allocator: expose per-model KV residency and estimated eviction cost to scheduler (owner: SRE infra)
Observability: add metrics (preemptions, preemption latency, kv-evictions, per-customer fairness index) and dashboard (owner: Observability)
E2E tests: mixed-workload scenarios, canary plan, and rollback automation (owner: QA)
Performance run: 72-hour soak in staging with mixed customers and adversarial long streams (owner: Performance)
Docs & SDK: API knobs for customer policies and guidance on labeling latency-sensitive traffic (owner: DX)
Rollout: staged canary across dedicated pools with feature flag gating (owner: Ops)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Avery Chen: Initial design completed. Key idea is to treat each active request as a 'ticket' with a token budget; when a ticket exceeds its short-term budget and a higher-priority ticket is pending, scheduler issues a soft-preempt at token boundary and parks the request. We will avoid hard evictions unless GPU memory is within critical threshold.

2026-02-18 - PM review (Rhea Patel): PM asked for clearer customer-facing policy semantics and fallback behavior when KV rehydration cost is high. Suggested adding a per-customer 'kv-sticky' flag to protect hot-conversations that are costlier to rehydrate.

2026-02-24 - Design review notes (Infra team): Raised concern about KV cache pointer consistency on preempt/resume across shards. Action: add a lightweight checkpoint of KV slab offsets and a guard in resume path to verify expected addresses; if mismatch, trigger safe re-sync and charge the customer for rehydration cost in logs.

2026-03-01 - Mateo Rivera: Simulator results v1: under mixed synthetic workload (60% short requests, 30% medium, 10% long), p95 for short class decreased by 18% while throughput dropped 4%. KV eviction rate increased by 14%—within target. Need to reduce preemption wake-ups (context switches) by batching preemption windows to token-aligned micro-windows (5-token granularity).

2026-03-04 - Security (Leah Ortiz): No PII exposure risk identified in scheduler. Recommended adding an audit log entry for preemption events (customer, reason, memory signal) for compliance checks. Marking S/R not required for code changes but ops will maintain sign-off for private deployments.

2026-03-08 - QA (Ben Carter): E2E tests created and passing in CI. Found a flaky test where resumed requests occasionally duplicate final tokens when preemption happens during streaming flush; root cause is double-flush in the transport layer. Added guard to transport flush path and added deterministic repro test.

2026-03-11 - Performance (Anika Bose): 24-hour staging soak: no OOMs, p95 short class improved 16%, overall token throughput within 2% of baseline. Observed KV eviction rate spikes when many long streams resumed simultaneously after preemption windows — plan to stagger resume backoffs and add jittered rehydration delay.

2026-03-12 - Mateo Rivera: Merged prototype PR to feature-flag gate. Next: enable canary on two dedicated pools next week, monitor metrics, and iterate on resume jitter/kv-sticky heuristics. Open item: finalize billing/charge implications for customers with high rehydration costs (PM follow-up).
